operations.name: Sidney Resnick

expected.name: Sidney Resnick
expected.description: Sidney Sussman Resnick was a New Haven printer and Connecticut Labor Youth League leader prosecuted in the New Haven Smith Act case. Arrested May 29, 1954 in the Connecticut Smith Act roundup. On June 16, 1954, he remained in New Haven County Jail because he could not raise bail; the previous day his bail had been reduced from $20,000 to $10,000. He was subsequently released on bail, and a February 23, 1955 court ruling confirms that all seven original defendants were then at liberty. His exact jail admission and release dates, and total time detained, remain unverified. On March 29, 1956, the jury could not reach a verdict in his case; the charges were subsequently dismissed.
expected.body:
Documented pretrial detention

Arrested May 29, 1954 in the Connecticut Smith Act roundup. On June 16, 1954, he remained in New Haven County Jail because he could not raise bail; the previous day his bail had been reduced from $20,000 to $10,000. He was subsequently released on bail, and a February 23, 1955 court ruling confirms that all seven original defendants were then at liberty. His exact jail admission and release dates, and total time detained, remain unverified.

Sources: Manchester Evening Herald, June 16, 1954, page 14, “State Reds Unable To Raise Cut Bail”; United States v. Silverman, February 23, 1955, 129 F. Supp. 496, 514; UConn Archives, original seven-defendant leaflet (May 29 arrest date and identities).

United States Attorneys Bulletin, April 13, 1956, page 247: jury disagreement on March 29, 1956; National Guardian, September 23, 1957: charges dismissed after a hung jury.

operations.source: Family obituary published by Weller Funeral Home: https://www.wellerfuneralhome.com/obituaries/sidney-resnick . Exact dates explicitly listed. Identity confirmed through New Haven printing career and1954SmithAct arrest among seven Connecticut communist leaders, not Cornell mathematician Sidney Ira Resnick. Generic dove memorial image inspected and rejected as a portrait.
